root_causes.description: The frontend service exhibits a severe p99 latency spike (~10,000ms) that is intrinsic to the frontend itself. All eight downstream dependencies (checkout, payment, product-catalog, recommendation, cart, shipping, currency, ad) show normal p99 latency (<25ms), frontend CPU (0.02 cores), memory (~214MB), and pod restarts (0) are normal, error rate is 0, and slow traces (user_checkout_multi ~15s) complete with 'ok' status. This indicates an application-level latency fault in the frontend request path rather than downstream propagation or resource exhaustion.

evidence.expected_baseline: p99_latency_ms < 100ms (all sibling services measured 1.98-24.85ms in same window)
p99_latency_ms < 100ms — rules out checkout as latency source

evidence.observed_value: user_checkout_multi trace duration=15021ms, status=ok; search_traces found 15 traces >5000ms, 0 with errors, p95_duration=190527ms
evidence.expected_baseline: user_checkout_multi traces typically complete in <1s with ok status
error_rate=0 — rules out http_abort; pure latency fault

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage=0.020 cores (mean=0.019, p50=0.020, max=0.020), flat with no spike

evidence.expected_baseline: memory_usage well below frontend limits — rules out memory_stress

evidence.observed_value: no logs found — no error logs from frontend during incident window
evidence.expected_baseline: no error logs expected; consistent with error-free slow responses

root_causes.description: Downstream dependency failure was considered but ruled out: every service the frontend calls (checkout, recommendation, product-catalog, cart, shipping, currency, ad) and their transitive dependencies (payment, email, quote) show normal p99 latency, and the slow frontend traces contain zero errors, so the 10s delay cannot be attributed to a failing or slow dependency.

evidence.observed_value: user_checkout_multi trace duration=15027ms, status=ok — slow but error-free
evidence.expected_baseline: traces complete <1s; dependency failures would surface as errors/timeouts

root_causes.description: Resource exhaustion (CPU or memory stress) on the frontend pod was considered but ruled out: frontend CPU usage is flat at 0.02 cores, memory working set is stable at ~214MB, pod restarts are 0, and no Kubernetes events (OOMKilled, BackOff) were found for the frontend pods during the window.

evidence.observed_value: cpu_usage=0.020 cores flat (mean=0.019, max=0.020), no spike
evidence.expected_baseline: cpu_stress would show sustained usage near/exceeding CPU limits

evidence.observed_value: memory_usage stable at ~214MB (max=214446080 bytes), no growth trend
evidence.expected_baseline: memory_stress would show monotonic growth toward the container limit

evidence.observed_value: no K8s events found (no OOMKilled, BackOff, or FailedScheduling events)
evidence.expected_baseline: resource stress or crash loops would produce OOMKilled/BackOff events

remediation_steps: Check for active chaos/fault-injection experiments targeting the frontend pod (e.g., network delay or app-level latency injection) and terminate them if found.
Inspect the frontend deployment config and recent changes for artificial delays, blocking calls, or misconfigured timeouts in the request handler path.
Restart the frontend deployment (kubectl -n otel-demo rollout restart deployment/frontend) to clear any transient in-process latency fault.
Verify frontend outbound connection pool, thread pool, and lock contention settings that could cause request queuing.
Add a p99 latency SLO alert on the frontend service (threshold ~500ms) for faster detection of recurrence, and confirm recovery by re-querying frontend p99 after remediation.
